notes: Account background: B2B fintech platform providing real-time transaction recommendations and customer-facing chat; high regulatory bar for EU and NA customers.
Executive ask (CTO): 'We need guaranteed throughput for peak windows and p95 latency under 200ms for 32-token generation across the production surface.'
Why Redwood: they like unified API + dedicated pools; previous experiments with other providers saw unpredictable tail latency and token cost variance.
POC scope agreed: 3-week Dedicated POC focused on throughput guarantees, latency SLOs, reserved GPU planning, and SLA language.
POC test plan (high level):
- Week 1: baseline perf on hosted models (small-scale) to set expectations
- Week 2: full load tests against Dedicated pool (steady-state throughput, rps sweep, concurrency matrix)
- Week 3: soak test (48h at 80% of target), failover scenarios, and SLA verification (p95/p99 measurements + billing impact for breaches)
Representative workloads: customer chat (avg 48 tokens), fraud reranking (batch of 16 candidates per request), profile embeddings (512-d vectors, high qps).
Target metrics defined by customer:
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/s for chat endpoints (avg 48 tokens) across 8 regions, burst to 300 req/s for 5 min
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 600ms for chat generation (32-64 token responses), 95th percentile reranking latency < 450ms
- Availability/SLA: 99.9% preferred, open to 99.95% with pricing delta; explicit credit schedule requested.

Initial infra ask: evaluate two reservation plans: (A) 4x H100-equivalent GPUs with aggressive batching + KV warm caches; (B) 8x A100-equivalent focused on lower-latency per-request routing. Internal debate: cost vs tail latency.
Test configuration notes (SE input):
- Use continuous batching with max batch size 16 for chat, tune timeout to 5ms to avoid extra head-of-line latency.
- Pre-warm KV cache using synthetic priming traffic mimicking 70% repeat prefixes.
- Measure cold-start penalty for model variants and for route failover to cheaper quantized models.
Observed early numbers (Week 1 hosted run):
- Baseline p95 hosted: ~270ms for 32-token chat on upstream model at single-region; p99 spikes >1.2s under moderate concurrency.
- Customer conclusion: hosted won't meet SLOs; Dedicated required if we can't deliver tail improvements.
SLA negotiation items to resolve:
- Definition of 'downtime' vs 'degraded performance' (do latency breaches count toward credits?)
- Credit calculation: customer insists on credits for p99 breaches during peak windows; Redwood prefers credits tied to availability only.
- Scheduled maintenance windows and notification SLA.
Risk & contingency plan:
- Fallback routing: policy to fall back to a lower-cost quantized variant for non-critical flows during overloads; must preserve accuracy thresholds.
- Regional failover: replicate pool capacity across 2 NA regions for planned maintenance and AZ-level failures.
Open technical questions for Redwood team:
- Recommended GPU mix and sizing given their per-request latency target and the reranking batch workload? (Priya requested a proposal with perf curves)
- Can we enforce hardware pinning and predictable kernel selection to reduce p99 jitter?
- How does Redwood compute 'sustained throughput'—is it a rolling 5m average or 1h? Need explicit definition for contract.
Sales/Legal asks: provide an SLA draft that includes p95/p99 measurement methodology, incident credits, and performance SLO acceptance tests for signing POC success.
